Passed on the fake backend by `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/samdejong86__agilent33600 --backend fake` (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. Publish review remains required by the card. NOT COVERED: the arbitrary-waveform sample array. UploadArb.py:82 sends the samples as a little-endian float block through pyvisa write_binary_values; the declarative SCPI bridge has no binary block, so the SOUR1:DATA:ARB block and the waveform file's samples are not implemented. The scalar channel-1 settings around it (frequency, voltage, offset, function, arbitrary-waveform name, arbitrary sample rate) are implemented, together with the *IDN? identity read and the SYST:ERR? error queue. The read query forms (SOURCE1:FREQUENCY? and the others) are the SCPI query form of the set commands the clone shows; the clone itself only queries *IDN? (AgilentControl.py:43) and SYST:ERR? (AgilentControl.py:73), so the exact queries were not exercised upstream. The SQU and TRI function tokens are shown on channel 2 in squareWave.awg:1 and triangleWave.awg:1; the driver applies the same function tokens to channel 1. No frequency, amplitude, offset or sample-rate range is stated in the clone (README.md:10 points to an external manual that is not part of the clone), so those four numeric writes are Limit.operator_required and are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until an operator overlay supplies a bound. site-limits.example.json is only an example acceptance overlay, not a device specification. Risk is R1: the clone shows low-voltage outputs (0.07 V, 0.2 V, 0.5 V) and no high-voltage or high-energy text; the card floor is R0. The e-stop writes SOURCE1:VOLTAGE 0, setting the one output value the driver controls (channel-1 amplitude) to zero; it is a software stop, not a hardware safety function, and the clone shows no output-off command (only OUTPUT1 ON in arb.awg:11). The card's entry symbols are module-level VISA resource objects (AgilentControl.py:24, UploadArb.py:65), not Python classes; the package is a ScpiDriver, whose G7 check inspects the command tokens of the SCPI transport rather than a native class surface, and `native` records AgilentControl:inst. The upstream README's only install step is `pip install pyvisa-py` (README.md:17-19); this package declares no install commands because the SDK's hardware SCPI backend uses a stdlib TCP socket or an operator-supplied VISA resource. The clone has no LICENSE file and the card records license_spdx NOASSERTION and license_class unknown; no upstream code is copied into this package. The fake is an in-memory transport, not a recording; every start value and canned reply is marked # placeholder in fake.py.
